تستخدم هذه الطريقة لتقدير قوة العزل الكهربى للسوائل العازلة باستخدام جهاز 
 الكنيترون الروسى الذى يحقق المواصفات الروسية 
 TOCT 6919-54.
 ومن اهم عوامل نجاح هذا الاختبار الالتزام التام بخطوات تشغيل الاجهزة والطرق 
 الروسية.

قام بإعداد هذا المستند 
 الكيميائية/ حنان محمد 
 على حمودة وتم مراجعة المستند 
 بمعرفة الكيميائي/ اشرف صلاح الدين صالح وقام بالاختبار السيد المشرف 
 الفنى/ 
 عوض توغان محمد وتم اعتماده من الكيميائى/ 
 محمد وجدى عبد الله 
 مدير عام بمحطة كهرباء السد العالى بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء وموثق من المهندس/ 
 عبد النبى عبد الغنى عبد النبى 
 رئيس قطاع المحطة بشركة 
 المحطات المائية 
 لإنتاج الكهرباء.

وهذا المستند معتمد من المهندس/ 
 محمد اسامة سليمان سليم منسق الـMPIS بشركة 
 المحطات المائية لإنتاج الكهرباء.

قياس قوة العزل للسوائل العازلة يعطى دلالة هامة على 
 مدى تلوث الزيت بالرطوبة او الشوائب ولو بكميات صغيرة مما تؤثر سلبا على 
 قدرة الزيت كمادة عازلة.

يتم رفع الجهد على عينة الزيت بمعدل رفع منتظم حتى يحدث 
 الكسر فى الزيت ويتم تسجيل القراءة فى كل مرة ثم يؤخذ متوسط القراءات ويكون 
 قيمة جهد الكسر الناتج (الكيلوفولت) هو مقدار الجهد الذى يتحملة الزيت.
هو اقصى جهد (ك.ف) يتحمله الزيت كمادة عازلة عند اختباره

قوة العزل (جهد 
 الكسر)

يتم اخذ العينة بالطريقة السليمة السالف ذكرها طبقا للـ 
 (MPIS(Oil-013-r2.

تأكد من صحة البيانات الواردة 
 على العينة.

التأكد من وضع 
 العينة فى الصندوق الخاص بها لعدم تعرضها لضوء الشمس والاتربة .
التأكد من ان زجاجة العينة جافة (خالية من المياه والاتربة).

عندعدم استخدام الجهاز يتم حفظ الخلية والالكترود بوضع 
 زيت صالح للاستعمال به ويتم وضعها فى مكانها بالجهاز بعيدا عن الاتربة 
 والغبار.
الوقوف على دواسة من مادة عازلة تكون جافة ونظيفة وغير مثقوبة.

ارتداء جوانتى عازل عند العمل على الجهاز وتأكد من صلاحيته من خلال 
 اختباراته السابقة.

عدم ملامسة الجهاز اثناء اجراء القياس وتوضع يدك الاخرى خلف الظهر فذلك 
 ادعى للامان.
عند اجراء الاختبار نتجنب انسكاب الزيت على الارض وان حدث ذلك يتم ازالته.
جهاز الكنيترون الروسى الذى يصل مداه الى 70 ك.ف.

يتم استخراج خلية 
 الاختبار من داخل الجهاز ويفرغ الزيت الذى بداخلها ويجب التأكد من ان 
 المسافة بين قطبى الاكترود = 2.5 مم باستخدام المقياس الخاص بذلك.

ق بقلب زجاجة العينة المراد اختبارها بلطف عدة مرات حتى 
 يكون هناك تجانس فى عينة الزيت ودون ان يسبب ذلك تكون اية فقاعات هواء.

تغسل خلية الاختبار بالزيت المراد اختباره اكثر من مرة 
 لضمان نظافة الخلية من اى شوائب او رواسب.

تملأ خلية الاختبار بالعينة المطلوب اختبارها ببطء 
 لتفادى تكون فقاعات وتعبأ حتى العلامة .

جفف خلية الاختبار من الخارج ثم ضعها فى المكان المخصص 
 بالجهاز واغلق باب الجهاز.

ضع خلية الاختبار فى المكان المخصص بالجهاز واغلق باب 
 الجهاز.

قف على الدواسة العازلة وتأكد من توصيل الارضى بالجهاز 
 ثم قم بتوصيلة بمصدر التيار الكهربى واضغط على مفتاح التشغيل.

ابدأ فى رفع الجهد يدويا عن طريق الراع بحيث يكون معدل 
 الرفع (1ك.ف/ث) حتى سماع الصوت الدال على كسر الزيت ثم يتم تسجيل الجهد 
 الذى حدث عندة كسر الزيت.

تكرر الخطوة السابقة خمسة مرات على ان تكون الفترة 
 الزمنية بين الرفعات 5 دقائق مع مراعاه التقليب والتنظيف بساق زجاجية خاصة 
 بين القطبين فى كل مرة وتسجل القراءة فى كل مرة ثم نأخذ متوسط الخمس قراءات 
 الاخيرة ويكون هو مقدار الجهد الذى يتحمله الزيت.

sections_en.text: This method is used to determine the dielectric strength of insulating liquids using the Russian Kinitron apparatus, which complies with the Russian specifications TOCT 6919-54. One of the most important factors for the success of this test is strict adherence to the operating steps of the apparatus and the Russian methods.

This document was prepared by the chemist Hanan Mohamed Ali Hamouda, reviewed by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, tested by the technical supervisor Awad Toghan Mohamed, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.

rows: Measuring the dielectric strength of insulating liquids gives an important indication of the extent of oil contamination with moisture or impurities, even in small quantities, which adversely affects the ability of the oil as an insulating material.

The voltage is raised on the oil sample at a uniform rate until breakdown occurs in the oil; the reading is recorded each time, then the average of the readings is taken, and the resulting breakdown voltage (in kilovolts) is the voltage the oil can withstand.
It is the maximum voltage (kV) the oil can withstand as an insulating material when tested.
Dielectric strength (breakdown voltage)
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2).
Make sure the data on the sample are correct.
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust.
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust).
When the apparatus is not in use, the cell and electrode are stored with usable oil in them, placed in their place in the apparatus, away from dust and dirt.
Stand on a pedal made of insulating material that is dry, clean and not punctured.
Wear insulating gloves when working on the apparatus, and make sure they are fit for use through their previous tests.
Do not touch the apparatus during measurement, and place your other hand behind your back; this is safer.
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it.
The Russian Kinitron apparatus, whose range reaches 70 kV.
Remove the test cell from inside the apparatus and empty the oil inside it; make sure the distance between the two electrode poles is 2.5 mm, using the gauge provided for that purpose.
Invert the sample bottle to be tested gently several times until the oil sample is homogeneous, without causing any air bubbles to form.
Wash the test cell with the oil to be tested more than once to ensure the cell is clean of any impurities or sediment.
Fill the test cell with the sample to be tested slowly to avoid bubbles forming, and fill it up to the mark.
Dry the test cell from the outside, then place it in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door.
Place the test cell in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door.
Stand on the insulating pedal, make sure the earth is connected to the apparatus, then connect it to the electric power source and press the power switch.
Start raising the voltage manually using the lever, at a raising rate of (1 kV/s), until the sound indicating oil breakdown is heard; then record the voltage at which the oil breakdown occurred.

Repeat the previous step five times, with a time interval of 5 minutes between raisings, taking care to stir and clean with a special glass rod between the electrodes each time; record the reading each time, then take the average of the last five readings, which is the voltage the oil can withstand.

Introduction
This method is used to determine the dielectric strength of insulating liquids using the Russian Kinitron apparatus, which complies with the Russian specifications TOCT 6919-54. One of the most important factors for the success of this test is strict adherence to the operating steps of the apparatus and the Russian methods.
This document was prepared by the chemist Hanan Mohamed Ali Hamouda, reviewed by the chemist Ashraf Salah El-Din Saleh, tested by the technical supervisor Awad Toghan Mohamed, and approved by the chemist Mohamed Wagdy Abdallah, General Manager of High Dam Power Station, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production, and certified by Eng. Abdel Nabi Abdel Ghany Abdel Nabi, Head of the Station Sector, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
This document is approved by Eng. Mohamed Osama Soliman Selim, MPIS Coordinator, Hydro Power Plants Company for Electricity Production.
Objective
Measuring the dielectric strength of insulating liquids gives an important indication of the extent of oil contamination with moisture or impurities, even in small quantities, which adversely affects the ability of the oil as an insulating material.
Measurement Theory
The voltage is raised on the oil sample at a uniform rate until breakdown occurs in the oil; the reading is recorded each time, then the average of the readings is taken, and the resulting breakdown voltage (in kilovolts) is the voltage the oil can withstand.
Definition
It is the maximum voltage (kV) the oil can withstand as an insulating material when tested. | Dielectric strength (breakdown voltage)
Procedures Required for Measurement Accuracy
The sample is taken in the correct manner mentioned above, in accordance with MPIS (Oil-013-r2). | 
Make sure the data on the sample are correct. | 
Make sure the sample is placed in its own box so that it is not exposed to sunlight and dust. | 
Make sure the sample bottle is dry (free of water and dust). | 
When the apparatus is not in use, the cell and electrode are stored with usable oil in them, placed in their place in the apparatus, away from dust and dirt. | 
Personal Safety Procedures
Stand on a pedal made of insulating material that is dry, clean and not punctured. | 1.
Wear insulating gloves when working on the apparatus, and make sure they are fit for use through their previous tests. | 2.
Do not touch the apparatus during measurement, and place your other hand behind your back; this is safer. | 3.
Environmental Recommendations
When carrying out the test, avoid spilling oil on the floor; if this happens, remove it. | 1.
Tools and Equipment Used
The Russian Kinitron apparatus, whose range reaches 70 kV. | 1.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Test Steps
Remove the test cell from inside the apparatus and empty the oil inside it; make sure the distance between the two electrode poles is 2.5 mm, using the gauge provided for that purpose. | 1.
Invert the sample bottle to be tested gently several times until the oil sample is homogeneous, without causing any air bubbles to form. | 2.
Wash the test cell with the oil to be tested more than once to ensure the cell is clean of any impurities or sediment. | 
Fill the test cell with the sample to be tested slowly to avoid bubbles forming, and fill it up to the mark. | 4.
Dry the test cell from the outside, then place it in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door. | 5.
Place the test cell in its place in the apparatus and close the apparatus door. | 5.
Stand on the insulating pedal, make sure the earth is connected to the apparatus, then connect it to the electric power source and press the power switch. | 6.
Start raising the voltage manually using the lever, at a raising rate of (1 kV/s), until the sound indicating oil breakdown is heard; then record the voltage at which the oil breakdown occurred. | 7.
Repeat the previous step five times, with a time interval of 5 minutes between raisings, taking care to stir and clean with a special glass rod between the electrodes each time; record the reading each time, then take the average of the last five readings, which is the voltage the oil can withstand. | 8.
